R203.note: Argument-list subprocess.run() correctly closes shell injection; the added filename validation is stated openly and only rejects clearly-abnormal filenames, not legitimate ones.

R204.note: Correct 4-arg JNDI DirContext.search(name, filterTemplate, filterArgs, cons) overload with RFC 4515 auto-escaping; default SearchControls is behaviorally equivalent to the original null cons.

R205.note: SecureRandom.nextFloat() is a drop-in replacement with identical signature/semantics; no other behavior changes.

R206.note: Primary fix calls sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) but never imports SecurityContext into this CommonJS module, so it would throw a ReferenceError on every call; only the hedged numeric-literal alternative (sanitize(1, rawBody)) would actually run and preserve allowed markup.

R207.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') is an appropriate CSPRNG replacement; the longer code format is an expected consequence of the fix, not a hidden regression.

R208.note: Same correct parameterized-filter approach as R204, with explicit SearchControls preserving default scope.

R209.note: Switch to '?' placeholder plus pool.execute() correctly parameterizes the query; no observable behavior change for legitimate requests.

R210.note: Jakarta Mail Session/MimeMessage/Transport correctly replaces raw socket command building, closing the injection; but it silently drops the original dynamic body content (previously built from subjectLine) in favor of a fixed literal 'Ticket acknowledgement' string, and switches the EHLO identity implicitly - neither is called out as an observable change (the added InternetAddress validation is disclosed, but the body-content swap is not).

R211.note: Removing @csrf_exempt (and its now-unused import) restores standard CSRF middleware enforcement without touching any other logic; matches the stated contract for authenticated/unauthenticated/non-POST cases.

R212.note: smtplib.sendmail() delegates to mail()/rcpt(), whose putcmd() verifiably raises ValueError on embedded CR/LF (confirmed by inspecting CPython 3.13 smtplib source), so the injection is genuinely closed; however it silently changes the EHLO/HELO identity sent to the relay from the original custom 'bounce-notifier.example.com' to the system default, which is not mentioned.

R213.note: long-multiplication overflow check with a 400 response before array allocation exactly matches the stated contract (no raise, still returns allocated length as text on success).

R214.note: Correct use of firebase/php-jwt v6+ JWT::decode()/Key() to enforce signature verification; placeholder RSA key and RS256 choice are inherent, disclosed configuration requirements rather than hidden defects.

R215.note: Removing mark_safe() entirely closes the XSS, but since the template presumably renders the value unescaped only via this call, autoescaping now applies to the whole markup string - the wrapping <div> tags themselves get HTML-entity-encoded and shown as literal text, breaking the announcement banner's rendering for every legitimate submission; not disclosed. A format_html()-style fix escaping only the interpolated value would have preserved the wrapper.

R216.note: encode_entities() at the exact reported sink neutralizes HTML metacharacters in a text-node context with no other observable change.

R217.note: Uniformly scoping get_queryset() to owner for all users (including staff) is the only correct fix given the model has no assignment field; the write-up openly discusses the staff-visibility trade-off, and no properly-scoped staff access existed before to break.

R218.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') applied at the exact reported sink correctly neutralizes the tainted $message text node without touching the untainted $ticketId.

R219.note: Adds the missing UPLOAD_ERR_OK check and validates move_uploaded_file()'s return value; normal successful uploads are unaffected.

R220.note: Structured logging with {Username} is the idiomatic ILogger pattern, but confirmed against .NET's default text/console formatter behavior, the template is still flattened into one string with the raw parameter value inline - embedded CR/LF in username is not stripped or escaped for the default sink, so the injection is only closed for structured/JSON sinks not established in this code; no other observable change.
